conventions.convention: AC is assumed for the inherited conditional-expectation existence interface; conditional expectations are almost-sure classes with measurable integrable versions. Completeness of the conditioning sigma-algebra is not required.
The conditional-error guarantee is under one fixed null law P₀. The adapted rejection event includes any eventual rejection, including early and final decisions.

The selected sample size N is interim-measurable and takes values in a nonempty subset of the positive integers. Calibration is required for every selected-size stratum, every interim event H, and every fixed u ∈ [0,1].

The random threshold A is an interim-measurable representative taking values in [0,1] everywhere. Conditional superuniformity is assumed separately at each fixed threshold; no common exceptional set over all real thresholds is assumed. Rejection uses p₂ ≤ A.
The normal example uses independent standard-normal stage statistics and c > 0. The adapted weights are (1,0) when Z₁ ≥ 0 and (0,1) when Z₁ < 0, retaining the original critical value c.

load_bearing.statement: Assume AC. Under one fixed null probability law P₀ and interim sigma-algebra F₁, let R₀ be the original rejection event and R₁ the adapted event of any eventual rejection. Choose A = E₀[1_R₀ | F₁] and Q = E₀[1_R₁ | F₁]. For α ∈ [0,1], if P₀(R₀) ≤ α and Q ≤ A almost surely, then P₀(R₁) ≤ α.

Under the conditional-error theorem's hypotheses, choose an F₁-measurable conditional-error representative A valued everywhere in [0,1]. If measurable p₂ ∈ [0,1] satisfies E₀[1_{p₂≤u} | F₁] ≤ u almost surely for every fixed u ∈ [0,1], then R₂ = {p₂ ≤ A} satisfies E₀[1_R₂ | F₁] ≤ A almost surely, and hence P₀(R₂) ≤ α.

Assume AC. On a probability space with interim sigma-algebra F₁, let N be F₁-measurable with values in nonempty M ⊆ ℕ_{>0}, and let p_N be the measurable selected stage-2 p-value. Put D_m = {N=m}. If P₀(H ∩ D_m ∩ {p_N ≤ u}) ≤ uP₀(H ∩ D_m) for every m ∈ M, fixed u ∈ [0,1], and H ∈ F₁, then E₀[1_{p_N≤u} | F₁] ≤ u almost surely for every fixed u ∈ [0,1].
